run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T17:09:22Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by 5xx/failed ingress spans at the proxy that trace to cart's inability to reach its Redis backend. frontend-proxy produced 811.8 STATUS_CODE_ERROR 'ingress' spans in the 16 minutes to 17:25:26Z versus 2016.5 UNSET, while its 'router frontend egress' spans carried 0 errors (evidence 18cdf87a-ca0b-44a5-955b-b8e2c9d0c54a-t0:9d297790-4b40-4867-bc7d-c61cdcd77b8b, d266273e-ccf8-4d5a-a314-c62ef88dfe1f-t0:eb84cd1e-0367-48df-b414-2f57fb900e18). Error spans at the proxy begin at the 17:09:22Z bucket (0 before, then 64, 137, 119, 140, 124 per 2m) (31346360-310c-4406-998e-88f038522e0a-t0:11f9b0af-7b14-4f0f-8357-13aa4ee15587). The failing proxy spans are 15.0-second ingress spans with http.status_code 504 whose frontend child spans also last 15.0s, i.e. proxy timeouts on slow upstream answers (6abf206d-fab8-42e3-abab-fb595b1b1eb9-t0:87f82392-fef1-40d9-a8a5-5bcf843bb086). Downstream, cart's own error spans and logs give the exact diagnostic: 'Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' from ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected(), for POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and GetCart, with span durations of 454-480 s (34e7f85f-e9e5-49b1-bb90-b872dbd6de7c-t0:f3d181a7-dd77-49dc-a48f-a14c5df6fc8a). The cart pod logged normal GetCartAsync traffic until 17:09:39Z and the first 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' at 17:09:41Z, repeating through the end of the log window (6267e76f-4fe7-436c-99b4-b291f65e3f23-t1:9ca073a4-1eea-4dcf-8b20-0c98fc966297). Those cart errors surface at the frontend as http.status_code 500 on /api/cart with grpc '9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage ... Wasn't able to connect to redis', and at checkout as oteldemo.CartService/GetCart errors (6abf206d-fab8-42e3-abab-fb595b1b1eb9-t1:cfa23d08-628b-4fb3-88fb-93021b6f6c5e). The redis that cart is configured to use is valkey-cart:6379 (VALKEY_ADDR), and its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, ~3.9 MB working set against a 10Mi limit, 0 memory-fail increments and 0.6-6.7% CFS throttling, so no valkey-side resource failure or restart is observable; however valkey-cart emitted no retrievable logs, so whether the redis process itself stopped answering, or the cart-to-valkey network path broke, is not established. Pod restarts, OOM, node pressure, DNS and CNI agent failures were checked and found not to be the trigger.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded 811.78 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on span_name 'ingress' and 2016.53 STATUS_CODE_UNSET in the 16 minutes to 2026-11-16T17:25:26Z, while span_name 'router frontend egress' had 0 error spans over the same window.

frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans were 0 per 2m through the 17:07:22Z bucket, then 64 at 17:09:22Z and 137, 119, 140 and 124 per 2m in the following buckets, i.e. the error burst starts around 17:08-17:09Z.

The failing proxy requests are timeouts: in trace 8c60daa4d9a9ea84f4e8115583a8f868 the frontend-proxy 'ingress' span 4900a517c13a3ee6 lasted 15,000,246 us with error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR, its child 'router frontend egress' span 762b52dc75cb8de1 lasted 15,000,078 us with error="true" and http.status_code=0, and the frontend 'POST' span ffbc76740906ff04 beneath it lasted 15,000,055 us.

cart's error spans carry the exact diagnostic 'Status(StatusCode="FailedPrecondition", Detail="Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' raised in cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() line 97, on operations POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, with durations of 454,082,185-479,682,021 us.

Pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logged normal 'GetCartAsync called with userId=...' lines up to 17:09:39Z, then logged 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' at 17:09:41Z and repeatedly (every few seconds, matching a ~4-5 s connect timeout cadence) through 17:15:58Z.

cart stopped completing work after onset: its STATUS_CODE_UNSET span count fell from ~1200-2100 per 2m to 377 at 17:09:26Z and 0 from 17:10:26Z onward, while STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans appeared from the 17:12:26Z bucket (13.3, 10.1, 10.7, 16, 32, 13.3, 18.7 per 2m).

frontend's own failures are on the cart path: 'GET /api/cart' and 'POST /api/cart' spans return http.status_code=500 with grpc.error_message '9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis', and checkout's oteldemo.CartService/GetCart spans are also in error.

cart's redis target is the valkey-cart service: cart container env is VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, Service valkey-cart is ClusterIP with port 6379 selecting opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart, and Endpoints valkey-cart currently holds address 100.96.2.228 for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr with no notReadyAddresses.

Neither container restarted: cart container is running with restartCount 0 since 2026-11-16T16:36:21Z, valkey-cart container is running with restartCount 0 since 2026-11-16T16:36:19Z, and both have an empty lastState.

valkey-cart showed no resource-exhaustion signal of its own: working set grew only from 3,481,600 to 3,878,912 bytes against a 10Mi limit, container_memory_failcnt increase over the window was 0, CPU usage stayed ~0.0017-0.0036 cores and CFS throttle ratio stayed ~0.011-0.067, so no OOM or CPU starvation of the redis container is observable.

cart's own container CPU rose from ~0.006-0.011 cores to 0.022-0.032 cores and its CFS throttle ratio rose from 0.12-0.27 in the 16:47-17:09 buckets to 0.72-0.94 at 17:11-17:17, making it the most throttled pod in otel-demo (0.845 over 16m, next highest postgresql at 0.389).
All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, including i-0146cb0d0caf26bae where both the cart pod and the valkey-cart pod run.

DNS and CNI control-plane pods are healthy in their current state: both coredns pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 (started 2026-11-12), and all five cilium-agent pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, including cilium-kvgq8 on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae.

The only events in otel-demo inside the window are about a previous cart pod: Pod/cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s 'Stopping container cart' (Normal/Killing, count 75, last 17:12:12Z) and a Warning/FailedKillPod at 17:12:11Z with 'failed to "KillContainer" for "cart" ... DeadlineExceeded' (count 30); the current cart pod belongs to ReplicaSet cart-755465879b owned by Deployment cart, and ReplicaSet cart-9fd895bb7 no longer exists.

Resource limits are uniformly small across the whole otel-demo namespace (e.g. product-catalog cpu 15m/mem 30Mi, image-provider 5m/15Mi, frontend-proxy 30m/50Mi), so cart's 45m/165Mi and valkey-cart's 10m/10Mi are within the cluster's normal range; neither cart nor valkey-cart defines a readiness or liveness probe.

Pod crash, OOMKill or container restart as the trigger is rejected: both cart and valkey-cart containers have been continuously running since 16:36:19-16:36:21Z with restartCount 0, empty lastState, and 0 memory-fail increments, and no Evicted or OOMKilled event exists in the window.

Node-level resource pressure as the trigger is rejected: every node is Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure False, and other pods on the same node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (e.g. product-catalog, CFS throttle 0.094 with 96-143 us server spans) were serving normally while cart was failing.

cart's CPU throttling (cpu limit 45m) as the initiating cause is not supported: cart was already throttled 0.12-0.27 while serving ~1200-2100 spans per 2m before the incident, its usage was only ~0.010 cores of the 45m limit, and the first 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' line at 17:09:41Z precedes the 0.72-0.94 throttle buckets seen from 17:11:22Z, so the throttling is more consistent with a consequence of the redis retry load than with the trigger.

Leading candidate for the deepest cause: the valkey-cart redis backend stopped answering new connections from cart around 17:09Z, so every cart Redis operation failed and cart stopped completing requests. Support: cart's only failing dependency is redis (exact error text from EnsureRedisConnected), valkey-cart is the configured VALKEY_ADDR endpoint, and no other object in the chain shows an independent failure. Unresolved: valkey-cart's pod is Ready with no restart, low CPU/memory and an empty memory-fail counter, and its logs could not be read, so whether the redis process itself stopped accepting connections (e.g. blocked event loop or maxclients) is not verified.

Alternative candidate still open: the pod-to-pod network path between cart (100.96.2.233) and the valkey-cart endpoint (100.96.2.228), both on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, broke at ~17:08Z. Support: cart's connect attempts time out on a ~4-5 s cadence and no 'connection refused' text appears, which is consistent with dropped packets rather than a closed port; counter: no direct drop/deny evidence is available and both cilium-agent on that node and the cluster DNS pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

Alternative candidate still open: cart's own StackExchange/redis client entered an unrecoverable reconnect loop (client-side fault) under high concurrency, independent of valkey's health; the ~4-5 s repeated connect failures and 454-480 s span durations fit reconnect backoff, but no client-internal state (connection pool, reconnect counters) is exposed by the available metrics, so this cannot be separated from a server-side cause.

Before any change, capture valkey-cart's own state on pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr (redis INFO: connected_clients, blocked_clients, maxclients, event-loop latency) and its container logs, since the decisive question is whether the redis process stopped accepting connections or the packets never arrived.

Separately from the redis connectivity fault, cart's CFS throttling reached 0.85-0.94 during the incident and neither cart nor valkey-cart defines readiness or liveness probes, so reviewing the cart cpu limit (45m) and adding probes would improve detection of a wedged cart instead of relying on downstream 504s at frontend-proxy.

gaps: valkey-cart's application logs could not be read for the window: fetch_pod_logs on pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr returned status no_data with 0 lines for both instances, so whether the redis process reported errors, refused connections or was blocked is unknown.

No redis-server metrics (clients, blocked clients, maxclients, evictions) and no packet-drop/Cilium-Hubble telemetry are available in this Run, so neither a valkey-internal stall nor a network-path fault between cart and valkey-cart can be confirmed or excluded.

kube-state metric series were absent for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready, kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and kube_pod_container_info in this window (queries returned no_data), so it is unknown whether valkey-cart or cart was ever not-ready during the incident; only cAdvisor container metrics and the current object state were available.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule itself was not retrievable: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name RequestErrorRate and an empty rule list overall, so the alert's exact expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown; the reported alert value 1.0888 could not be reproduced, and the observed proxy error share is expressed only as error spans (811.78 of 2828.31 ingress spans over 16m), which is not a request-level error rate.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, configuration, node or network-policy change can be correlated with the ~17:08Z onset.

The cause of the previous cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s remaining in termination with FailedKillPod/DeadlineExceeded events (counts 30 and 75, last at 17:12:12Z) is unknown and its relationship, if any, to the redis connectivity loss could not be established.
No trace or metric evidence was found tying the small error counts at ad and fraud-detection (1.03 error spans each over 16m) to this incident; they are left unexplained rather than attributed.
next_steps: Inspect valkey-cart pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr interactively (redis-cli INFO clients/stats/latency, SLOWLOG) to determine whether it was refusing, blocking or accepting connections at 17:08-17:25Z.

Capture connectivity evidence between pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 (100.96.2.233) and the valkey-cart endpoint 100.96.2.228:6379, for example Hubble flow/drop records or a debug pod running 'nc -z -v -w5 valkey-cart 6379' on the same node.
Review whether valkey-cart's limits (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi) and the absence of readiness/liveness probes on cart and valkey-cart are intentional for this environment.

Check with the owners of the otel-demo namespace whether any change was applied around 2026-11-16T17:08Z (deployment, network policy, valkey memory/maxclients configuration), using a change-history source not available here.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration to confirm which metric and threshold produce the reported value 1.0888.

Alternative candidate still open: the pod-to-pod network path between cart (100.96.2.233) and the valkey-cart endpoint (100.96.2.228), both on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, broke at ~17:08Z. Support: cart's connect attempts time out on a ~4-5 s cadence and no 'connection refused' text appears, which is consistent with dropped packets rather than a closed port; counter: no direct drop/deny evidence is available and both cilium-agent on that node and the cluster DNS pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

Alternative candidate still open: cart's own StackExchange/redis client entered an unrecoverable reconnect loop (client-side fault) under high concurrency, independent of valkey's health; the ~4-5 s repeated connect failures and 454-480 s span durations fit reconnect backoff, but no client-internal state (connection pool, reconnect counters) is exposed by the available metrics, so this cannot be separated from a server-side cause.

recommendation.text: Before any change, capture valkey-cart's own state on pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr (redis INFO: connected_clients, blocked_clients, maxclients, event-loop latency) and its container logs, since the decisive question is whether the redis process stopped accepting connections or the packets never arrived.

Separately from the redis connectivity fault, cart's CFS throttling reached 0.85-0.94 during the incident and neither cart nor valkey-cart defines readiness or liveness probes, so reviewing the cart cpu limit (45m) and adding probes would improve detection of a wedged cart instead of relying on downstream 504s at frontend-proxy.

counter_evidence.text: valkey-cart showed no resource-exhaustion signal of its own: working set grew only from 3,481,600 to 3,878,912 bytes against a 10Mi limit, container_memory_failcnt increase over the window was 0, CPU usage stayed ~0.0017-0.0036 cores and CFS throttle ratio stayed ~0.011-0.067, so no OOM or CPU starvation of the redis container is observable.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Pod crash, OOMKill or container restart as the trigger is rejected: both cart and valkey-cart containers have been continuously running since 16:36:19-16:36:21Z with restartCount 0, empty lastState, and 0 memory-fail increments, and no Evicted or OOMKilled event exists in the window.

Node-level resource pressure as the trigger is rejected: every node is Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure False, and other pods on the same node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (e.g. product-catalog, CFS throttle 0.094 with 96-143 us server spans) were serving normally while cart was failing.

cart's CPU throttling (cpu limit 45m) as the initiating cause is not supported: cart was already throttled 0.12-0.27 while serving ~1200-2100 spans per 2m before the incident, its usage was only ~0.010 cores of the 45m limit, and the first 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' line at 17:09:41Z precedes the 0.72-0.94 throttle buckets seen from 17:11:22Z, so the throttling is more consistent with a consequence of the redis retry load than with the trigger.
